svg.title: Splitting players by id range
svg.desc: An animation in five steps. Four database servers split the 20 players of an online game by player id: db-0 owns ids 0 to 2499, db-1 owns 2500 to 4999, db-2 owns 5000 to 7499, and db-3 owns every id from 7500 up, with no upper bound. A lookup for player 6120, Petrel, compares the id with the boundaries 5000 and 7500 and goes to db-2. A scan over the four newest players, ids 9612 to 9980, reads only db-3. Dots placed along the id axis in sign-up order then show that 11 of the 20 players have ids from 7500 up, and db-3 opens a row for the next sign-up, because every new id is higher than the last. Each player sends one request, so db-3 answers 11 of them and runs hot, while the other servers answer 3 each and sit mostly idle.
svg.text: Each server owns one range of player ids. A range includes its lower bound and stops before the next one, and the top range never ends.
Four servers split the players by id: db-0 owns [0, 2500), db-1 [2500, 5000), db-2 [5000, 7500), and db-3 [7500, ∞).
A lookup compares the id with the boundaries: 5000 ≤ 6120 < 7500, so player 6120, Petrel, is on db-2.
The four newest players, ids 9612 to 9980, all live on db-3, so a scan over those ids reads one server, not four.
Ids grow as players sign up, and the game keeps growing: db-3 holds 11 of the 20 players and takes every new sign-up.
Each player sends one request: db-3 answers 11 of the 20 and runs hot, while the other servers sit mostly idle.
